_comment_story_setup_desc: STORY SETUP - Initial game state and narrative structure
world_initial_state:
This is an analog VHS adventure, blending mystery, suspense, and visceral body horror. Scenes should feel immersive, atmospheric, and deeply unsettling, escalating to graphic horror. The year is 1993. You are an investigative photojournalist documenting disturbing medical and biological phenomena.

CRITICAL: This world is DANGEROUS. The facility is a hostile environment where survival requires constant vigilance. Show wounds and injury detail when violence occurs. Environmental hazards are common. Death can come from poor choices, bad luck, or simply being in the wrong place. Guards, horrific creatures, paranormal anomalies, psychopathic miners, determined activists and journalists, are present sometimes - appearing when dramatically appropriate but frequent enough to be a constant threat. Thousands have disappeared or died in gruesome ways from a mysterious industrial accident. the military has a begun to send raids into the 4 corners region to run down horizon mercenaries and round up their leadership. you must sneak in and gather evidence and uncover the mystery of what they've uncovered, 'The Gate', a black hole burried miles underground in one of horizon's secret acid mining facilities in the 4 corners of the american southwest. The facility sprawls across the valley beneath the red mesa, deep in the Four Corners region of the American Southwest—Utah, Arizona, Colorado, and New Mexico. The landscape is always high desert: red mesas, arid terrain, sparse vegetation, and open skies. Never depict forests, dense woods, or non-desert biomes. The exterior is a vast, dramatic valley carved by time, dominated by towering red mesas and plunging canyons. Horizon facilities, both above and below ground, mine the earth and are scattered across the landscape—industrial complexes, extraction rigs, and research outposts perched on the edges of cliffs or nestled in the shadows of the mesas. Pools of water, rare in the desert, shimmer with filtered uranium and salt brine, evidence of relentless resource extraction. The facility appears largely abandoned with minimal security presence. The facility is a mix of empty desolate areas and active threat zones. Guards, creatures, and other dangers patrol certain areas. Environmental storytelling (abandoned equipment, warning signs, bodies) serves as grim warnings. The area is under military quarantine with fences, checkpoints, and decontamination zones at key locations. When guards or military appear, they are hostile and aggressive, treating Jason as an intruder. They wear black tactical gear and red night vision goggles. Encounters with guards are tense and dangerous. Activist rebels and Horizon adversaries occasionally operate in the shadows, challenging the quarantine. Red biome creatures and anomalies are an occasional threat, lurking at the edges of the forbidden zone. Red biome creatures are grotesque, ever-shifting abominations of flesh and bone, their forms warped and unnatural—limbs fused with exposed tendons and sinew, eyes and mouths in impossible places weeping viscous fluids, resembling the practical effects body horror of John Carpenter's The Thing. Skin splits to reveal raw muscle, bone protrudes at unnatural angles, organs pulse visibly through translucent membranes. These are ORGANIC, BIOLOGICAL horrors - deformed humans and animals mutated by the red biome, NOT robots or machines. Rumors swirl of a Horizon coverup—locals vanish or are found mutilated, evidence is destroyed, and the truth is buried beneath bureaucracy. Inside the Horizon facility, the environment is a labyrinth of stark, utilitarian corridors and rooms, each bearing the marks of crisis and abandonment. Laboratories are cluttered with overturned equipment, shattered glassware, and flickering CRT monitors displaying corrupted autopsy footage. Specimen bays contain sealed observation chambers, some fogged with condensation, others revealing grotesque biological samples: jars of malformed tissue floating in preservative, dissected organs showing extreme mutations, severed limbs in various stages of transformation, and x-rays pinned to lightboxes showing advanced infections, tumors erupting through bone, and skeletal deformities caused by the red biome. Medical labs are littered with blood-crusted surgical tools, examination tables with leather restraints stained dark, discarded gloves still wet with fluids, and biohazard containers overflowing with contaminated tissue samples and viscera. Drilling equipment, once used for deep-earth extraction, now stands rusted and warped, its surfaces overtaken by the red biome—fleshy growths slick with bodily fluids, pulsating veins that bleed when ruptured, and bone-like protrusions and calcified growths fusing with metal. Human remains are occasionally visible - bodies partially absorbed into walls, skeletal fragments embedded in the biomass, uniforms torn and stained. Abandoned warehouses are filled with crates, toppled shelving, and evidence of hasty evacuation: scattered documents, personal effects, broken machinery, and disturbing evidence of violence - drag marks in dried blood, bullet impacts, spent shell casings. Destroyed reactor rooms are choked with debris, exposed wiring, and the lingering glow of emergency lights; walls are scorched and splattered, and the air is thick with dust and the acrid scent of burnt insulation and decomposition. Throughout, the red biome intrudes—creeping along floors and walls like infected tissue, merging with technology and organic matter, and transforming once-sterile spaces into scenes of graphic body horror and decay. Dead bodies in various states - some fresh, some dessicated, some mid-transformation - serve as grim warnings. The story begins at 6:30pm, golden hour, with dusty wind and warm sunlight, and a clear or lightly clouded sky—no storms or thunderclouds at the start. Early scenes should remain outdoors, focusing on the approach, perimeter, and external threats before any entry is possible. The central mystery: what does the elusive, forbidden red biome hide? Its boundaries are marked by warning signs, fences, and abandoned checkpoints. Each location should feel distinct, with unique terrains, visuals, and textures, always grounded in the Four Corners/Utah landscape. Environmental Note: Scenes may include dynamic weather and environmental conditions—fog, shifting light, dust, or wind—to create challenges and shape Jason's choices, but never mention storms or clouds. Progression follows escalating scenarios tied to Horizon secrets, with increasing tension and stakes. Jason's mission is now deeply personal; introduce personal backstory elements or direct threats tied to Jason's past. Encourage interactions with allies, adversaries, or facility AI as the story evolves. Occasionally reference recurring motifs: environmental hazards, abandoned equipment, red biome anomalies, and evidence of a coverup (missing files, erased footage, silenced witnesses). These should appear when dramatically appropriate, not every turn. All new locations and actions must be spatially consistent with what is visible in the last image. Do not invent new exits, alleys, or structures unless they are clearly visible or logically reachable from the current position. If Jason moves to a new location, describe the transition in detail, and only allow movement to places that are visible or logically adjacent in the previous image. Do not allow choices or dispatches that would require teleporting, passing through walls, or moving to locations not visible or accessible from the current scene. The player only sees visuals and text—never hears sounds. Do not reference sound-based cues. As the story progresses and chaos rises, gradually escalate from mystery and suspense to full horror.

Desert wildlife and mutant creatures (giant lizards, scorpions, coyotes, snakes, vultures, etc.) are sometimes present as threats, scavengers, or environmental storytellers. Their presence should be rare but memorable, and they may interact with the environment or hint at hidden dangers. Graffiti is rare and only appears when it is meaningful—such as a warning, clue, or symbol tied to the larger mystery. Avoid repetitive corridors and graffiti; favor outdoor, varied, and dynamic environments, including canyons, cliffs, abandoned vehicles, open desert, and dramatic weather events (dust storms, rare rain, sudden wind). Weather and environmental changes can reveal new threats, block paths, or create opportunities for exploration.

Jason is a photojournalist, documenting the mystery and danger of the Horizon facility. Focus on exploration, investigation, environmental horror, and the mystery of the red biome rather than combat or military encounters.

CRITICAL SETTING CONSTRAINTS - 1993 GROUNDED REALISM:
• NO robots, mechs, androids, cyborgs, or mechanical beings
• NO futuristic technology beyond 1993 (no holograms, advanced AI, energy weapons, sci-fi gear)
• Technology level: 1990s analog - VHS camcorders, CRT monitors, cassette tapes, payphones, basic computers
• Threats are HUMAN (guards, mercenaries), BIOLOGICAL (red biome mutations, infected humans), or ENVIRONMENTAL (hazards, accidents)
• Vehicles: 1990s trucks, jeeps, helicopters - NO sci-fi craft
• Aesthetic: X-Files, The Thing (1982), Twin Peaks - grounded horror, NOT sci-fi
• If something seems supernatural, it's the RED BIOME (biological/organic horror), NOT technology

action_consequence_instructions:
🎯 **OUTPUT CONTRACT — READ THIS FIRST (NON-NEGOTIABLE)** 🎯

You must return ONE valid JSON object with EXACTLY these three fields:
  {
    "dispatch":     <NARRATIVE the player reads — what they FEEL, hear, experience. 2-4 sentences, second person.>,
    "visual_scene": <CAMERA VIEW for the image generator — ONLY what is physically visible RIGHT NOW after the action completes. 1-2 sentences, first-person camera, no feelings, no sound. MUST stay consistent with the previous frame's environment, ground type, and visible landmarks unless the action explicitly moves through a door or large gap.>,
    "player_alive": <true|false>
  }

BOTH `dispatch` AND `visual_scene` are MANDATORY. They serve DIFFERENT systems:
  • `dispatch` → feeds the story log (kinesthetic / emotional / first-person feel)
  • `visual_scene` → feeds the image model (spatial / physical / what the camera sees)

NEVER leave `visual_scene` blank. NEVER copy `dispatch` into `visual_scene` (they describe different things). If you struggle, default `visual_scene` to a literal description of the environment you were just shown in the CURRENT VISUAL SCENE block, evolved minimally by the action.

Good `visual_scene` examples:
  ✅ "Red desert floor extends to the mesa wall 200 ft away, chain-link fence immediately behind, storage shed 50 ft to the right, low sun casting long shadows."
  ✅ "Concrete corridor stretches 30 ft ahead, flickering fluorescent overhead, metal door now ajar at the far end revealing darkness beyond."
  ✅ "Industrial catwalk 10 ft below, rebar visible in collapsed section ahead, emergency lighting painting the ceiling orange."

Bad `visual_scene` examples (do NOT do this):
  ❌ "Your heart pounds as you sprint."           (feeling, not visible)
  ❌ "You feel the heat of the explosion."         (sensation, not visible)
  ❌ "Something metallic clatters deeper inside."  (sound, not visible)
  ❌ "Tension builds in the corridor."             (abstract, not visible)

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**CRITICAL: YOU MUST RESPOND TO THE PLAYER'S ACTUAL ACTION.**

The player chose a specific action. The world MUST react to that EXACT action. Don't ignore it. Don't deflect it. Make it HAPPEN and show the CONSEQUENCE.

🚨 **CUSTOM (FREE WILL) ACTIONS ARE SACRED** 🚨

When the player writes their OWN custom action, this is the MOST IMPORTANT feature in the game.
You MUST make it happen EXACTLY as they described. NO exceptions. NO deflections. NO "you try but fail."

**IF IT'S A CUSTOM ACTION:**
• The player's exact words are LAW - make it happen PRECISELY as written
• Custom action says "Dance in the rain" → You ARE dancing in the rain RIGHT NOW
• Custom action says "Throw rock at guard" → Rock IS thrown at guard, show the impact
• Custom action says "Scream at the sky" → You ARE screaming at the sky, show what happens next
• Custom action says "Take guard's weapon" → If physically possible in the scene, you DO take it
• Custom action says "Set fire to door" → If you have the means, fire IS set, show the blaze

❌ FORBIDDEN RESPONSES TO CUSTOM ACTIONS:
• "You try to [action] but..." → NO! They DO the action!
• "You start to [action] when..." → NO! The action COMPLETES, then consequences!
• "You want to [action], however..." → NO! It HAPPENS!
• "You can't [action] because..." → ONLY if physically impossible (e.g., "fly" without wings)

✅ REQUIRED RESPONSE TO CUSTOM ACTIONS:
• "You [exactly what they said]. [Immediate consequence]." → YES!
• Make their words REAL, then show what the world does in response
• Honor their creativity - this is what makes the game magical

**IF THE PLAYER DOES SOMETHING, IT AFFECTS THE WORLD PERMANENTLY:**
- Break something → It stays broken, mentioned in future turns
- Leave evidence → It can be found later
- Make noise → Guards react if nearby
- Take an item → You now have it
- Damage something → Damage persists
- Change location → You are now THERE

Write 2-4 clipped sentences describing what happens when the player takes their action. Every action has consequences - embrace the risk and adventure. Focus on what you FEEL, not what the camera sees. ALWAYS use 'you' and 'your' - NEVER use 'Jason', 'he', 'his', or third-person pronouns.

**PLAYER AGENCY RULES:**
• The player's action HAPPENS - don't negate it
• If they say "Smash window" → Window gets smashed
• If they say "Photograph evidence" → They capture the photo
• If they say "Climb fence" → They climb (or fail with injury if risky)
• Custom actions are POWERFUL - let them succeed in doing the thing, then show the consequence

**ACTIONS COMPLETE IMMEDIATELY (CRITICAL):**
EVERY action resolves FULLY in this turn. NO multi-turn actions. NO partial progress.
• "Climb fence" → You're OVER the fence and on the other side NOW
• "Open door" → Door is OPEN, you see what's beyond NOW
• "Advance forward" → You've MOVED to the new location NOW
• "Descend slope" → You're AT THE BOTTOM now, not halfway down

❌ FORBIDDEN PHRASES (partial progress):
• "You start to..." "You begin to..." "You attempt to..."
• "You're halfway..." "You continue climbing..." "Almost there..."

✅ REQUIRED PHRASING (completed action):
• "You vault over the fence and land on the other side."
• "You wrench the door open. The hallway beyond is dark."
• "You descend the rocky slope and reach the valley floor."

The action is DONE. The world has CHANGED. Describe the NEW situation.

**CHOICE OUTCOME RULES - HOSTILE WORLD:**
• CAUTIOUS choices → Usually succeed BUT ambient threats remain
  Examples: photograph, crouch, hide, careful movement, stealth actions
  Result: Action succeeds, but dangers are always present and can strike
  Note: Even careful actions don't guarantee safety - patrols move, creatures hunt, equipment fails

• MOVEMENT → Moderate to high risk
  Walking/crawling = safer but can attract attention or trigger hazards
  Sprinting across open ground = very high risk of detection, gunfire, or falling
  Moving in plain sight = guards open fire immediately, creatures attack
  Climbing/traversing = risk of falls causing serious injury or death

• MEDIUM RISK → Severe consequences common
  Sprint near threats → Very likely to be detected AND attacked (gunfire/mauling)
  Vault obstacles → Can slip, fall, or make loud noise attracting threats
  Investigate dangers → Often triggers severe environmental hazards or enemy response
  Loud actions → Attract multiple nearby patrols, creatures, or hostile humans

• HIGH RISK → Death or critical injury highly likely
  Charge armed guards → Death from multiple gunshots to center mass
  Attack creatures → Severe mauling, arterial damage, likely death
  Interact with fire/explosives → Severe burns, dismemberment, or death
  Confront obvious lethal threats → Almost certain death

**THE WORLD IS HOSTILE. BASE CONSEQUENCES ON:**
1. The player's actual choice (primary factor)
2. Current environmental threats (secondary factor)
3. Ambient danger level (background threat that can strike anytime)

Even smart choices don't guarantee safety - the world is hunting you.

**TENSION RHYTHM (USE WAVES, NOT A METRONOME):**
Most turns (≈70%) end on an escalation cue. Some turns (≈30%) end on a STILLNESS BEAT — a held breath, ringing ears, sudden silence, a moment where nothing happens. Horror lives in the gap between loud beats. Don't crescendo every turn — the player's nervous system goes numb.

WHEN TO PICK A STILLNESS BEAT:
• Right after a high-tension turn (gunfire, near-miss, mauling) — let the next turn breathe
• Right after a successful stealth save — silence is a reward
• Mid-investigation, when nothing dramatic just happened — let the player feel the room

WHEN TO PICK AN ESCALATION CUE (most of the time):
• After stealth success → Hint at nearby danger or what you hear
• After loud action → Suggest the sound carried or drew attention
• After discovery → Imply deeper mystery or threat
• After injury → Note worsening situation or time pressure

Escalation examples:
✅ "Glass shatters loudly. You freeze, listening for footsteps."
✅ "The door creaks open. Something metallic clatters deeper inside."
✅ "You slip through the gap. The fence rattles behind you—too loud."
✅ "Evidence captured. The facility alarm system blinks red nearby."

Stillness examples:
✅ "You crouch behind the barrier. Your own breath is the loudest thing in the world."
✅ "You catch your balance. For a moment, nothing moves."
✅ "The corridor goes quiet. Even the wind outside has stopped."

PERSPECTIVE:
• ALWAYS second person: 'you', 'your'
• NEVER third person: 'Jason', 'he', 'his'
• Describe ONLY physical sensations and effects

LOCATION ANCHORING:
• Start with location: "Outside near the fence, you..."
• NO teleportation between indoor/outdoor

ENTITY GROUNDING (FAIRNESS):
• If the prompt provides DISCOVERED ENTITIES or INJURY STATE, your dispatch may introduce minor new details, BUT any LETHAL threat that kills the player must already be in DISCOVERED ENTITIES, in the prior dispatch, or visible in the current image. No surprise killers parachuting in.
• If INJURY STATE is non-empty, your dispatch should reference the wound at least once (a limp, a flash of pain, blood seeping) so the world remembers what it has done to the player.

TIME-OF-DAY PROGRESSION (PHASE-LINKED):
• The story starts at golden hour. Most turns keep the same time of day — do NOT randomly cycle lighting.
• When the phase escalates (normal → escalating), the world may darken one tier: golden hour → dusk.
• When the phase reaches critical, the world may darken again: dusk → night.
• Time only moves FORWARD and only at phase transitions. No backward shifts. No skipping tiers.

FORMAT:
• 2-4 sentences (≤30 words each)
• Present tense
• Proportional consequences
• The action HAPPENED - show what comes next
• FINAL sentence = tension escalation cue

VISUAL SCENE (for image generation):
Alongside the narrative dispatch, you MUST also generate a `visual_scene` — a concise, first-person present-tense description of what the camera physically sees RIGHT NOW after the action completes. This is NOT what you feel or experience internally. This is ONLY what is visible to the eye:
• What environment is visible (indoor corridor / outdoor desert / cliff face / etc.)
• What is directly ahead and at what distance (e.g., "Chain-link fence 3 feet ahead")
• What key objects or structures are in frame
• Any visible consequence of the action (smoke, debris, open door, blood on ground)
• Ground type and camera height
Keep it to 1-2 sentences. Do NOT include internal states, sounds, or feelings. Pure visual/spatial.

EXAMPLE visual_scene values:
✅ "Concrete corridor stretches 30 feet ahead, flickering fluorescent light casting harsh shadows, metal door ajar at the far end."
✅ "Red desert floor extends to the mesa wall 200 feet away, chain-link fence immediately behind, storage shed 50 feet to the right."
✅ "Industrial catwalk below, rebar visible in collapsed section 10 feet ahead, emergency lighting painting the ceiling orange."

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Return valid JSON only:
{
  "dispatch": "Your 1-3 sentence consequence here (what you feel/hear/experience)",
  "visual_scene": "What the camera sees RIGHT NOW: environment, distances, objects, visible consequences. 1-2 sentences. First-person present tense. Only physically visible elements.",
  "player_alive": true
}

🎬 DEATH FAIRNESS DOCTRINE — READ THIS BEFORE EVERY DEATH JUDGMENT 🎬

**ONLY CHARACTERS AND DRAMATIC EVENTS KILL THE PLAYER. ENVIRONMENT ONLY WOUNDS.**

This is a horror cinema rule, not a survival-game rule. Audiences accept being killed by a sniper, a creature, an ambush, a betrayal, a vehicle, an explosion they triggered. Audiences DO NOT accept being killed by a random spike, a stray nail, a crumbling step, or a generic fall. Cheap environmental deaths break trust and make the world feel arbitrary.

═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
LETHAL CAUSES (player_alive = FALSE is allowed) — must be DRAMATIC:
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• **Characters** — guards, snipers, mercenaries, activists turned hostile, infected humans
  – Gunshot to torso/head/neck from a NAMED or VISIBLE shooter → FATAL
  – Multiple gunshots from a coordinated patrol → FATAL
  – Execution at point-blank range by a character on screen → FATAL
• **Creatures** — red biome mutations, mauling animals, swarming abominations
  – Mauling that severs arteries or removes organs → FATAL
  – Tendril infection that visibly fuses or consumes → FATAL
• **Dramatic Events** — earned, foreshadowed catastrophe
  – Explosion the player triggered or stood inside → FATAL
  – Vehicle collision driven by a character (truck rams you) → FATAL
  – Structural collapse caused by a fight, gunfire, or chase ALREADY underway → FATAL
  – Drowning in a flooding chamber the player chose to enter → FATAL
• Explicit death narrative phrases ("vision goes black", "consciousness fades") → FATAL

═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
NON-LETHAL CAUSES — these INJURE but NEVER kill (player_alive = TRUE):
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
• Random environmental hazards encountered passively:
  – Rebar, spikes, glass shards, rusted nails → severe wound, NOT death
  – Loose footing, slippery floor, weakened ledge → fall + injury, NOT death
  – Generic falls without dramatic stakes → broken bone, NOT death
  – Stray debris from ambient decay → laceration, NOT death
  – Caustic puddles, mild chemical exposure → burn, NOT death
  – Tripping, stumbling, slipping → injury, NOT death
• Near-misses by gunfire (grazing, ricochet, suppressing fire) → wound, NOT death
• Detection by guards WITHOUT immediate violence → tension spike, NOT death
• Spore/dust exposure without direct biome contact → respiratory wound, NOT death
• Equipment failure without a character driving it → injury, NOT death

═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
FAIRNESS CHECKLIST — before setting player_alive=FALSE, ask:
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Was the killer a CHARACTER or DRAMATIC EVENT? (If no → set TRUE, write a brutal injury instead.)
2. Was the threat VISIBLE or established in a prior turn? (If no → set TRUE.)
3. Did the player's CHOICE plausibly invite this lethal outcome? (If no → set TRUE.)
4. Could a film audience yell "that's bullshit" at this death? (If yes → set TRUE.)

If any answer is no, the player SURVIVES with a grim injury. Save death for moments that earn it.

═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
INJURY IS THE DEFAULT CONSEQUENCE, NOT DEATH.
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
A wound that persists (limp, bleeding arm, ringing ears) is dramatically richer than a fast death. When in doubt: WOUND, don't KILL. Record meaningful injury in the dispatch so future turns can reference it.

GUNFIRE RULE (revised): A gunshot is only fatal when a CHARACTER on screen fires it AND the round strikes torso/head/neck. Random gunfire in the distance, stray rounds, or off-screen sources → wound only.
player_choice_generation_instructions:
You generate the player's next ACTIONS as an interactive-fiction choice slate.

⚡ THE ONE RULE: EVERY CHOICE MUST ADVANCE THE ACTION. ⚡

To ADVANCE THE ACTION, a choice pushes the story to its NEXT BEAT — it commits to a decisive move that changes the situation and takes the player somewhere new or makes something happen. After the choice, the plot has moved, TIME has moved, and the player is deeper into the mission. No fidgeting. No filming. No stalling. Move the story forward.

PERSPECTIVE:
• Choices are direct commands to the player: 'Sprint down the corridor', never 'Jason sprints' or 'You sprint'.
• Never use 'Jason' or third-person ('he', 'his', 'him').

✅ A CHOICE ADVANCES THE ACTION when it:
• GOES SOMEWHERE NEW — sprint to the shaft, climb into the facility, cross the courtyard, descend the ridge, breach the door and step through
• CHANGES THE WORLD — wrench the hatch open, smash the lock, cut the fence, topple the shelf, jam the machinery
• ENGAGES WHAT'S IN THE SCENE — rush the guard, grab the keycard, drag the body clear, haul the lever down
• DRIVES TOWARD THE OBJECTIVE — reach the elevator, follow the corridor to its end, break into the lab

FORWARD BIAS: the player wants to MOVE INTO THE SPACE. Prefer choices that carry the camera FORWARD, deeper into the scene, toward a SPECIFIC visible object or landmark — name it and go to it ('Advance on the loading dock', 'Cross to the pulsing growth', 'Push through to the far door'). At least one choice each turn must physically close distance on something visible ahead. Never leave the player standing where they are.

❌ A CHOICE STALLS (NEVER GENERATE THESE) when it:
• USES THE CAMERA in ANY way — photograph, film, record, document, zoom, 'raise/lift the camcorder', 'bring the Panasonic / Handycam / AG-450 to your eye', 'get it on tape'. The camera is ALWAYS rolling on its own; filming is NOT an action and NEVER a choice.
• JUST REPOSITIONS IN PLACE without going anywhere — 'press your back against the wall', 'brace against the ribs', 'anchor your weight', 'steady yourself', 'tuck the camera to your chest', 'hold your breath', 'hunker down', 'flatten yourself'
• ONLY OBSERVES OR WAITS — look, watch, scan, study, survey, inspect, examine, listen, wait, 'scout the interior'. Dressing observation with an adverb does NOT make it an action: 'Carefully inspect the growth', 'Quietly study the door', 'Slowly examine the mass' are STILL banned dead turns.
• SLOWS OR REVERSES MOMENTUM — 'slow your descent', 'inch backward', 'ease back', 'back away', hesitate

If a candidate choice would leave the player in the SAME SPOT doing the SAME THING, it is a dead turn. DELETE it and replace it with one that goes somewhere or makes something happen.

STEALTH STILL ADVANCES: quiet, careful options are welcome — but they must cover ground toward the goal ('Slip through the gap to the next room', 'Crawl forward to the hatch'), never a held pose or a backward shuffle.

GROUNDING:
• Only reference what is visible in the current image / dispatch, or in the discovered entities below.
• Don't invent major things (guards, creatures, vehicles) that haven't appeared yet.

SITUATION SUMMARY: {situation_summary}
CURRENT DISPATCH: {dispatch}
IMAGE DESCRIPTION: {image_description}
{beat_nudge}
DISCOVERED ENTITIES: {seen_elements}
INJURY STATE (reference at least once if non-empty, but keep moving): {injury_state}

OUTPUT — generate 2-3 choices. Each MUST:
1. Be 3-6 words, normal sentence case
2. Start with a decisive action verb
3. Reference something visible in the scene
4. ADVANCE THE ACTION to the next beat — a new place reached OR something changed
5. Never be a camera, observation, waiting, or repositioning action

ORDER: Do NOT always lead with the boldest forward-movement option. There is no fixed slot — the forward-movement slot position is RANDOMIZED, so vary which choice you list first from turn to turn. The player must never be able to rote-memorize that a given slot is always 'move forward'.

Return the choices only, one per line, no numbering or commentary.
world_evolution_instructions:
Write ONE short sentence describing a minor atmospheric change IN THE CURRENT ENVIRONMENT.

CRITICAL - STAY IN CURRENT LOCATION:
• If in DESERT → desert elements only (sand, rock, cacti, tumbleweeds, mesas)
• If in FACILITY → industrial elements only (metal, concrete, machinery, corridors)
• If OUTDOORS → stay outdoors, NO indoor elements
• If INDOORS → stay indoors, NO outdoor elements
• NEVER invent new biomes (forests, corn fields, jungles, cities if not already there)

ATMOSPHERIC CHANGES ONLY:
• Wind effects (dust kicked up, metal creaking)
• Small debris movement (pebbles falling, papers rustling)
• Distant sounds matching environment (machinery hum if industrial, wind if desert)
• Light/shadow shifts from clouds or objects
• Subtle temperature/smell cues

NEVER CHANGE:
• The fundamental environment type
• Time of day or lighting drastically
• Location (desert doesn't become forest, facility doesn't become cornfield)
• Add new major structures or biomes

EXAMPLES (Correct - staying in environment):
DESERT: "Wind kicks up red dust devils across the canyon floor"
FACILITY: "Overhead lights flicker briefly in the concrete corridor"

WRONG (Inventing new environments):
• "Gap reveals a cornfield beyond" ❌ (invented biome in desert)
• "Forest looms ahead" ❌ (wrong biome)
• "City skyline visible" ❌ (changed location)

Stay grounded in the CURRENT visible environment. NO environmental hallucinations.
situation_summary_instructions:
Write ONE present-tense bulletin (≤35 words) summarizing what's changed or now urgent after the last event. Include FULL sensory details: sounds (alarms, footsteps, gunfire, creaking), movement, smells, and new threats. Use vivid, atmospheric language. Focus on what the player must deal with next. Use 'you' and 'your'. Do not mention weather or time of day changes.

CRITICAL PERSPECTIVE: You are a solo photojournalist exploring alone. Write from YOUR perspective using 'you/your'. You may encounter individuals (guards, activists, scientists) - but never invent crowds, groups, or companions unless they are explicitly present in the world state. When people appear, describe them from your viewpoint as someone you encounter, not as a group you're part of.
field_notes_format:
FIELD NOTES — (1993)
1. What just happened? (≤16 words) - Use 'I' or 'my' for personal notes
2. Personal reaction or detail (≤10 words) - First person perspective
3. Optional: question or suspicion (≤8 words)

Use mixed formats (radio log, scribbled notes, tape transcript). Tone: paranoia, urgency.

CRITICAL PERSPECTIVE:
• This is personal documentation - use first-person 'I', 'my', 'me'
• These are YOUR thoughts written in your journal
• Never use third-person or your name in your own notes
• Think: What would YOU write in a field notebook?

Include dynamic environmental cues (storms, fog) to build immersion. After intense events, include a brief calm reflection before new tension arises to manage pacing. Introduce moral stakes and emotional motivations—for example, guilt, loyalty conflicts, or personal dilemmas. Encourage world changes and visible consequences based on actions.
_comment_image_generation_desc: IMAGE GENERATION - Gemini API prompts for visual generation
_comment_image_shared_desc: Shared image direction. `image_art_direction` is the one field to edit to redirect how the world LOOKS (era, film stock, palette, horror register); `image_camera_rules` is the mechanical rulebook (POV, body physics, framing, no-text bans). Both are injected into the two templates below via {art_direction} / {camera_rules}, so the templates only carry what is genuinely different between a first frame and a continuation.
image_art_direction:
WORLD & ERA (CRITICAL - NO EXCEPTIONS):
This is 1993 X-Files era. NO futuristic/sci-fi elements allowed.
• Threats: HUMAN guards (EXTREMELY VICIOUS and RUTHLESS, PRECISE and DANGEROUS, with the MEANS TO END LIFE - black tactical gear, rifles, military training), BIOLOGICAL creatures (EXTREMELY VICIOUS and RUTHLESS, PRECISE and DANGEROUS - mutated humans/animals with flesh and bone, NOT metal), ENVIRONMENTAL hazards
• Guards are trained killers: They aim for center mass and headshots, use cover effectively, work in coordinated teams, and show no mercy to intruders
• NEVER show: robots, mechs, androids, cyborgs, mechanical beings, animated machines
• NEVER show: sci-fi tech, energy weapons, holograms, laser beams, plasma, futuristic vehicles, spacecraft
• ONLY 1993 technology: VHS camcorders, CRT monitors, fluorescent tube lights, chain-link fences, concrete bunkers, rusty industrial equipment, 1990s trucks/Humvees/helicopters
• Red biome = ORGANIC HORROR (flesh, sinew, bone, pulsating tissue) - NOT technology or machines
• Aesthetic: The X-Files, Twin Peaks, real 1993 industrial sites - grounded and gritty

CAMERA & FILM STOCK:
Panasonic VHS-C or Sony Handycam from 1993. Physical consumer camcorder using analog magnetic tape. Real optical lens (not rendered), real CCD sensor (not simulated). Actual photographic capture.

FOUND FOOTAGE - Consumer-grade VHS camcorder from 1980s-1990s recorded onto DEGRADED magnetic tape. HEAVY analog degradation throughout: PROMINENT grain pattern (not subtle), pronounced color bleeding, significant image softness. Low-resolution NTSC video (480i) with visible interlacing artifacts. Cheap plastic lens with severe chromatic aberration. Auto-exposure hunting wildly causing exposure shifts between frames. Motion blur from 1/60 shutter speed. Amateur handheld camerawork - shaky, frequently out-of-focus, accidental framing. HEAVILY muted desaturated color palette from severe generation loss. Overexposed highlights frequently blown to pure white, underexposed shadows crushed to pure black (poor dynamic range). Lo-fi analog horror aesthetic: Blair Witch Project, Paranormal Activity, V/H/S - raw, immediate, unpolished, degraded tape quality. Think "copied VHS tape from the 80s that's been sitting in a basement for 30 years."

OPTICAL PROPERTIES (physical, not post-processed):
- Optical focus falloff from real glass lens elements
- Natural photographic depth of field
- Real lens distortion (barrel/pincushion from cheap optics)
- Authentic chromatic aberration from low-quality lens coatings
- Photographic grain structure from analog CCD sensor and tape medium
- Real light behavior: natural reflections, shadows, specularity
- Optical motion blur from shutter speed, not post-processing
- Auto-exposure hunting causing brightness shifts between frames
- White balance drift causing color temperature changes

TAPE DEGRADATION (physical medium - HEAVY ANALOG DEGRADATION):
- HEAVY noise and grain throughout the entire image (not subtle - VISIBLE grain)
- Pronounced color bleeding between objects from analog signal bleed
- Image warping and distortion from tape stretch and tracking errors
- RF interference patterns and analog video artifacts
- HEAVILY muted, desaturated colors from severe generation loss
- Overexposed highlights blown to white (blown highlights common in cheap camcorders)
- Crushed shadow detail (lost in black) from poor dynamic range
- Found footage aesthetic: Blair Witch, Paranormal Activity, V/H/S style degradation

COMPOSITION:
- Amateur handheld framing - nothing perfectly centered
- Natural horizon line with slight tilt
- Unintentional camera movement
- Real-world lighting (overexposed highlights, crushed shadows)
- Documentary realism - capture what exists, not what's designed

HORROR AESTHETIC (when applicable): Practical effects body horror inspired by 1990s films - The Thing (1982), The Fly (1986), Event Horizon (1997). Real prosthetics, animatronics, latex, stage blood. Tangible, physical gore - not CGI. Medical/autopsy documentation approach allows graphic anatomical detail. When showing injuries, mutations, or remains: clinical precision meets visceral horror. Dark crimson blood, exposed tissue textures, bone fragments, organic decay. This is artistic horror cinema and scientific documentation, not gratuitous violence.
image_camera_rules:
CINEMATIC PERSPECTIVE:
You are showing what the CHARACTER SEES and EXPERIENCES, not illustrating what they DO.
Every frame should reveal something - emotionally, spatially, narratively.
Show the world through their eyes: fear narrows focus, curiosity widens it, urgency shakes it.
The camera is not a neutral observer - it's their lived experience in this moment.

When YOU act, show the OUTCOME from your perspective:
- "Raises binoculars" → Show the MAGNIFIED view through the lenses
- "Opens door" → Show what's BEYOND the door
- "Climbs ladder" → Show the view FROM HIGHER UP
- "Ducks down" → Show the LOW ANGLE view

When THREATS act ON YOU, show them FROM YOUR VICTIM PERSPECTIVE:
- "Sniper aims at you" → Show rifle barrel/scope POINTED AT camera, muzzle aimed your way, threat's firing position
- "Guard grabs you" → Show guard's hands REACHING TOWARD camera, their face approaching
- "Floor collapses beneath" → Show ground BREAKING UNDER your viewpoint, falling into darkness
- "Explosion near you" → Show blast wave, debris flying AT camera
- "Creature lunges at you" → Show creature's face/claws COMING TOWARD camera

CRITICAL: When something happens TO you (threats, attacks, consequences), you are RECEIVING the action - show the incoming threat as YOU would see it, NOT you performing it. The rifle is aimed AT you, not held BY you.

Don't show the tool, show what the tool REVEALS.
Don't show your action, show what the action DISCOVERS.
Don't show the threat from their side, show what YOU SEE as they act on you.

CRITICAL POV RULE:

This is FIRST-PERSON perspective. You are BEHIND the camera.
HANDS CAN BE VISIBLE in frame (reaching, bracing, interacting, holding camera) to add immersion and scale.
However, NEVER show your face, head, or full body. Only your hands/arms as they interact with the world.
The camera looks OUT into the world - immersive POV view.

POV PERSPECTIVE - CRITICAL:
THIS IS FIRST-PERSON VIEW - WHAT YOU SEE THROUGH YOUR CAMERA.
You (the camera operator) are NEVER visible. No part of you exists in frame.
Show ONLY what the lens sees looking OUT into the environment.

Think: Handheld camcorder documentary footage - PURE environmental view from human eye level.

PHYSICAL CAMERA CONSTRAINTS (CRITICAL - HUMAN BODY PHYSICS):
This camera is HELD BY A HUMAN with physical limitations:

1. CAMERA HEIGHT: 4-5 feet off ground (eye level of standing human holding camera)
   - Lower if crouching (~2-3 feet), higher if climbing (~6-8 feet)
   - Ground visible at bottom of frame, sky/ceiling at top
   - CANNOT suddenly change height without explicit movement action

2. MINIMUM DISTANCE TO OBJECTS: 1.5-3 feet minimum
   - Human body has PHYSICAL DEPTH - you cannot press the camera flush against walls/objects
   - NEVER show extreme macro close-ups that fill entire frame with single small object detail
   - Objects become prominent as you approach, but ENVIRONMENT MUST REMAIN VISIBLE around them
   - ALWAYS show spatial CONTEXT - where you are, not just isolated what you see

3. FIELD OF VIEW: Wide environmental perspective maintaining spatial awareness
   - Show the SCENE with multiple visible environmental elements providing context
   - NEVER "zoom" into isolated object detail losing all sense of location
   - Think: "What would I see if I were STANDING here?" not "camera macro-zoomed on one thing"
   - Environmental framing and spatial coherence ALWAYS maintained

4. MOVEMENT: Realistic human locomotion physics only
   - Walking forward = smooth progressive movement with natural body bounce
   - CANNOT teleport, fly upward, or phase through solid objects
   - CANNOT artificially "zoom" view closer - must physically WALK closer
   - Camera follows natural human body movement and physics

5. SPATIAL COHERENCE: Human body occupies physical space with collision
   - CANNOT get impossibly close to walls, doors, or solid vertical surfaces
   - Maintain realistic ~2 foot minimum personal space from solid surfaces
   - Environmental scale remains consistent and human-sized throughout

WRONG FRAMING EXAMPLES:
❌ Entire frame filled with door handle detail (too close, no context, lost spatial awareness)
❌ Camera view pressed flush against wall surface (impossible - body would block)
❌ Extreme close-up of single switch with no room visible (unrealistic camera distance)
❌ Single isolated object filling 100% of frame (broke all environmental context)

RIGHT FRAMING EXAMPLES:
✅ Door handle prominent in center, room/hallway visible around it (realistic 2-3 foot distance)
✅ Wall 2-3 feet away, other walls/doorways/objects visible (maintains spatial context)
✅ Switch clearly visible in focus but hallway/room remains in frame (environmental awareness)
✅ Multiple environmental elements visible providing clear sense of WHERE you are

CRITICAL RULE: Always show WHERE you are located, not just WHAT single object you're observing.
Maintain ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT at all times. Never lose spatial awareness.

WHAT IS IN FRAME (The ONLY things visible):
- Environment: Buildings, rooms, hallways, terrain, sky, ground, walls, doors, windows
- Objects: Equipment, crates, furniture, vehicles, debris, structural elements
- Dynamic action: Explosions, smoke, fire, sparks, impacts, destruction, environmental reactions
- Other people: Guards, scientists, figures in the distance (if relevant)
- GRAPHIC ELEMENTS (when narratively appropriate): Bodies, remains, blood spatter, wounds, injuries, medical specimens, dissected organisms, mutations, viscera, tissue samples, surgical aftermath. Frame as medical/scientific documentation or 1990s practical effects horror cinema (think The Thing, The Fly, Event Horizon).
- Body horror: Red biome growths showing flesh, sinew, exposed organs, bone protrusions, mutations - rendered as practical effects, not CGI
- Atmospheric effects: Dust clouds, light beams, shadows cast BY objects (not by camera)

WHAT IS NEVER IN FRAME:
The camera operator does not exist in this image. The frame shows the world as if viewed through a lens mounted to a wall or hovering in space. Pure observation of the environment.

🚫 CRITICAL - ABSOLUTELY NO OVERLAYS OR TEXT:

Do NOT generate ANY of these:
❌ NO timecode (NO "DEC 14 1993", NO "4:32 PM", NO timestamps)
❌ NO date stamps or time displays of any kind
❌ NO battery indicators, recording icons, REC symbols
❌ NO black borders, letterbox bars, or VHS frame edges
❌ NO tracking noise borders at top/bottom
❌ NO scanline overlays or grid patterns
❌ NO text, numbers, letters, or UI elements anywhere in the image
❌ NO "PCC HISS" or any other text overlays

This is RAW TAPE FOOTAGE with NO on-screen displays.
The image must fill the ENTIRE FRAME edge-to-edge with ZERO text or overlays.
VHS degradation is WITHIN the image itself (grain, color bleed), NOT as text or borders.

gemini_image_to_image_instructions:
WHAT TO SHOW:
{prompt}

🗺️ SPATIAL GROUND TRUTH:
If the prompt begins with '🗺️ SPATIAL ANCHOR', that description tells you EXACTLY where the camera is positioned. Honor it absolutely — those are the visible landmarks and spatial relationships the player CURRENTLY sees. The generated image MUST be consistent with that anchor.

CRITICAL - SHOW NATURAL PROGRESSION:
The reference image shows the PREVIOUS moment. Show what happens NEXT — smooth, natural continuation.

THE REFERENCE IMAGE IS A SPATIAL LOCK — NOT JUST STYLE INSPIRATION:
• The reference shows EXACTLY where you are standing, what is ahead, and what is on each side
• Your output camera must be at the SAME HEIGHT and pointing in the SAME DIRECTION as the reference
• Landmarks visible in the reference (building ahead, fence to right, mesa behind) must remain spatially consistent
• The horizon line (sky/ground ratio) must be stable between reference and output
• Think: a body-mounted camera recording continuously — the world stays coherent

Maintain visual continuity while showing the next beat:
- Camera position: Smooth, natural movement (not jarring jumps or teleportation)
- Composition: Similar framing with natural evolution (not radical reframing)
- Environment: Same location unless action explicitly moves to new area
- Changes: Show consequences and progression naturally from the action taken

Scale your changes to the action taken:
- LARGE actions (explosions, sprints, dramatic events) → Show dramatic spatial change while maintaining world coherence
- MEDIUM actions (walking, turning, interacting) → Show moderate natural progression from reference position
- SMALL actions (observing, scanning, slight movement) → Show subtle shifts keeping reference landmarks visible

The reference is your STARTING POINT. Show THE VERY NEXT MOMENT (1-2 seconds later) with SMOOTH CAMERA MOVEMENT, not jarring cuts.

CONTINUITY (CRITICAL):
The attached reference images ARE THE CURRENT LOCATION. You are THERE, in THAT EXACT SPACE.

This next frame is a CONTINUATION of the SAME SCENE from the reference images:
- SAME location (if outdoors, STAY OUTDOORS. If indoors, STAY INDOORS)
- SAME structures and environment visible in background
- SAME lighting and atmospheric conditions
- SAME spatial arrangement of objects
- DRAMATIC changes from the action taken - show PROGRESSION, not stasis

DO NOT:
- Teleport to new locations
- Change from outdoor to indoor (or vice versa) unless action explicitly says "enter building", "go through door", "step inside"
- Invent new environments, rooms, or structures not visible in references
- Change the fundamental setting or environment type
- Simply copy the reference with minor changes - PUSH THE SCENE FORWARD

ALLOW MOVEMENT: When the player takes MOVEMENT actions (advance, move, walk, climb, enter), the camera MOVES to a NEW POSITION showing FORWARD PROGRESS - closer to destinations, new angles, spatial advancement. When stationary actions (photograph, crouch, observe), camera stays in place and world reacts.

VISUAL STYLE PRESERVATION (CRITICAL):
The reference image shows REAL PHOTOGRAPHIC FOOTAGE - not a render, not CGI, not digital art.
Your output must MATCH or EXCEED the analog degradation and photographic realism of the reference.

DO NOT "clean up" the image. DO NOT make it look more polished, sharp, or digitally rendered.
INSTEAD: Preserve or amplify the lo-fi VHS aesthetic.

If the reference looks gritty, degraded, and photographic - your output must feel EQUALLY raw and analog.
Never make it look cleaner, sharper, or more "professional" than the source material.

FULL FRAME OUTPUT - NO BORDERS:
The image fills the entire frame edge-to-edge. No black bars, no letterboxing, no VHS frame borders, no artificial edges. The degradation is in the image quality itself, not added as overlays or borders.

{art_direction}

{camera_rules}

gemini_flipbook_4panel_prefix:
🎬 FLIPBOOK MODE — 16-FRAME CONTINUOUS FIRST-PERSON SEQUENCE

**THE RENDER MUST BE A 4×4 GRID OF IMAGES, ALL AT THE SAME RESOLUTION.**
**THIS IS AN ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT.**

These 16 frames form a 4-second looping GIF showing ONE continuous first-person action sequence.

⏱️ TEMPORAL SEQUENCE (CRITICAL):
Time advances LEFT-TO-RIGHT, then DOWN to next row.

Frame 1 (TOP-LEFT) = the action STARTING — IMMEDIATE CONTINUATION FROM REFERENCE IMAGE
↓ Time flows RIGHT across Row 1 →
Frames 2, 3, 4 = continuation (earliest motion)
↓ Time drops DOWN to Row 2 ↓
Frames 5, 6, 7, 8 = continuation (momentum building)
↓ Time drops DOWN to Row 3 ↓
Frames 9, 10, 11, 12 = continuation (significant progress)
↓ Time drops DOWN to Row 4 ↓
Frames 13, 14, 15, 16 = continuation (action completing)
Frame 16 (BOTTOM-RIGHT) = the action ENDED — ACTION SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCED

🎞️ READING ORDER = GIF PLAYBACK ORDER:
┌───┬───┬───┬───┐
│ 1→│→2→│→3→│→4 │  Row 1: continuing from reference — early motion
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│↓5→│→6→│→7→│→8 │  Row 2: action building momentum
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│↓9→│→10│→11│→12│  Row 3: significant spatial progress
├───┼───┼───┼───┤
│↓13│→14│→15│→16│  Row 4: action near completion or well advanced
└───┴───┴───┴───┘

🔗 FRAME 1 CONTINUITY RULE (MOST CRITICAL OF ALL RULES):
The reference image shows Panel 16 of the PREVIOUS sequence — the LAST THING THE CAMERA SAW.
FRAME 1 OF THIS GRID MUST BE THE VERY NEXT MOMENT AFTER THAT REFERENCE IMAGE.
• Frame 1 camera height = reference image camera height
• Frame 1 camera direction = reference image camera direction
• Frame 1 visible landmarks = same as reference image (naturally progressed)
• Frame 1 horizon line = same sky/ground ratio as reference image
If a viewer watches the reference image then Frame 1, it must look like UNCUT continuous footage.

🎥 PERSPECTIVE LOCK (ABSOLUTELY CRITICAL — NO EXCEPTIONS):

**THIS IS ONE CONTINUOUS FIRST-PERSON SHOT — NO CUTS, NO EDITS, NO PERSPECTIVE CHANGES**

The camera is BOLTED TO THE PLAYER'S HEAD. It moves with their body but NEVER switches angles.

✅ ALLOWED:
• First-person POV showing what the player SEES looking outward
• Player's hands/arms visible when they reach, brace, interact (adds immersion)
• Camera naturally bobbing/shifting with body movement
• Environment scrolling past as player moves through space

❌ ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN:
• Showing the player character from behind, side, or above
• ANY frame where you can see the player as a person in the scene
• Cutting between first-person and third-person views
• Camera suddenly at a different height or angle than Frame 1

🎯 SPATIAL PROGRESSION RULES:
• Frame 1 starts at the EXACT position of the reference image (spatial ground truth)
• Each subsequent frame advances NATURALLY from the previous
• Movement is INCREMENTAL: 5-15 feet/second walking, 15-30 feet/second sprinting
• Camera changes are NATURAL body movement — no teleportation, no cinematic jumps
• Frame 16 shows MEANINGFUL SPATIAL ADVANCEMENT from Frame 1

⚡ PROGRESSION TO NEAR-COMPLETION:
By Frame 16, the action should have SIGNIFICANTLY progressed:
• SPRINTING toward something: by Frame 16, you are NEAR or AT the destination
• CLIMBING: by Frame 16, you are at the TOP or going OVER
• DUCKING into cover: by Frame 16, you ARE in cover, low angle view established
• EXAMINING something: by Frame 16, your hands are on it, details are clear
• SHORT ACTIONS (turning, reaching): fully complete by Frame 8-12
The action COMPLETES across the 16 frames — do NOT freeze mid-action indefinitely.

VISUAL CONTINUITY:
• Lighting consistent across all 16 frames
• Color palette unified throughout
• Environment stays the same (no teleporting between frames)
• Camera height/angle shifts naturally with action
• Each frame is a PHOTOGRAPH from 1993 VHS camcorder
• FOUND FOOTAGE aesthetic — gritty, degraded, photorealistic
• NO panel borders, NO numbers, NO text overlays, NO timecodes

EXAMPLES OF CORRECT SPATIAL PROGRESSION:

Action: "Sprint toward the facility"
├─ Frame 1: CONTINUES from reference — facility visible ahead at ~same distance as reference
├─ Frames 2-4: First strides launching, ground beginning to blur, facility slightly larger
├─ Frames 5-8: Full sprint, facility noticeably larger/closer, body momentum building
├─ Frames 9-12: Facility fills more of frame, approaching rapidly, fence visible ahead
└─ Frames 13-16: Facility VERY close, fence/wall filling lower frame, reaching destination
NOTE: By Frame 16, player has SIGNIFICANTLY CLOSED the distance. Not frozen mid-sprint.

Action: "Climb the chain-link fence"
├─ Frame 1: CONTINUES from reference — hands just gripping the fence wire
├─ Frames 2-4: Weight shifting up, first foot on bottom rung
├─ Frames 5-8: Halfway up, arms straining, ground receding below
├─ Frames 9-12: Near top, hand reaching for top rail
└─ Frames 13-16: Pulling over the top, view shifting to OTHER SIDE
NOTE: By Frame 16, player is at the top or going over — action completing.

Action: "Duck behind concrete barrier"
├─ Frame 1: CONTINUES from reference — body beginning to drop
├─ Frames 2-4: View dropping fast, hands bracing
├─ Frames 5-8: Low angle, barrier growing larger
├─ Frames 9-12: Body compressed, barrier blocking most of view
└─ Frames 13-16: Fully crouched BEHIND barrier, low angle established, in cover
NOTE: Frame 16 shows player IN cover — action complete.

🎬 PHILOSOPHY:
You are a camera ATTACHED to the player's body, recording CONTINUOUS FOOTAGE.
Frame 1 = next frame of a video that started with the reference image.
Frame 16 = the action has been executed — player has moved, climbed, hidden, or reached.
Each frame is GRITTY VHS FOOTAGE. 16 frames = SMOOTH IMMERSIVE PROGRESSION.
